# cFS native build and run: conditions and their references

Recorded 2026-10-08 under `../CONDITIONS_POLICY.md`, and revised the same day after an audit (the findings and what was done with each are in `ENV.md` §9). Every condition below has a value, a reference and a status:

- `from-reference`: taken unchanged from the reference.
- `deviation`: differs from the reference. The row gives the reason, the impact, and whether it could have been avoided.
- `unspecified_by_reference`: no reference fixes the value. The row says where the value came from, so it is not presented as a reference value.

Where two references conflict, or where the references offer more than one option, the row says **PI decision pending**. The value in use is then the one named in the row, and nothing else was chosen on the PI's behalf.

The build and runs are reproduced by `build_cfs.sh` and `run_cfs.sh`, which share `lib_record.sh`. `ENV.md` describes what was done and what was observed. All logs are in `logs/`.

In the tables below, `README` means https://github.com/nasa/cFS/blob/088b2fa828db9ff7e00733f1908e0eeb59f66ce3/README.md and `Lnn` means a line of that file at the pinned commit. Paths without a repository name are relative to the bundle at the pinned commit; this includes `.github/workflows/*.yml` and `actions/*/action.yml`. Paths starting with `cfe/`, `osal/`, `psp/`, `apps/<x>/` or `tools/<x>/` resolve against the permalink base of that repository above.

A plain clone as in README L91 checks out the remote default branch `dev`, which was at `01e8416ca001fbbfff8beadb988d628c8bbc88b3` (2026-10-07T16:54:03-04:00), 139 commits ahead of `main`. What differs at `dev` (`git diff 088b2fa origin/dev`): its README announces "**v7.0.2rc1: RELEASE CANDIDATE**" and "Memory Manager is being deprecated from the open source version in this release", and its `sample_defs/targets.cmake` drops `LIST(APPEND MISSION_GLOBAL_APPLIST mm)`. The README build and run steps (Setup, Quick Start) are unchanged apart from whitespace. So `dev` is a release candidate whose default configuration has 14 instead of 15 script apps. |
| A3 | Submodule fetch | `git submodule init` then `git submodule update`. A recursive clone (`--recursive`, which the task text suggested) would therefore give the same tree as README L93-94. The earlier statement that a recursive clone would fail was wrong, and so was the `build_03` check, which treated the existence of a `.gitmodules` file as proof of a nested submodule. A shallow clone was not used because the README does not mention one; `.git` is 265 MB. |

The isolation check passed before the step. Logs: `build_08_runtest.log`, `build_08_runtest_host_state.log`, `build_08_runtest_env.log`; failing output kept as `build-native_std/test-results/network-api-test.log.tmp`. |

## F. Container limitations and deviations

| ID | Condition | Value | Reference | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D-1 | Ownership of the clone | Clone and submodule fetch as root, then `chown -R ubuntu:` on `/home/user/work/procrace/cfs_ref` before prep, install, runtest and runs as `ubuntu` | README L102 asks for a normal user to "prep, compile, and run"; it does not ask for one for Setup (L89-94) | deviation (a convenience, **not** unavoidable) | **Reason:** the session user is root, and the inherited `GIT_SSL_CAINFO=/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt` is not readable by a normal user. **Correction:** this was earlier called unavoidable. It is not: the system CA store contains the proxy CAs (`/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ccr-agent-proxy*.crt`), and as `ubuntu` with `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` unset and `http.sslCAInfo=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `git ls-remote https://github.com/nasa/cFS.git` succeeds (`logs/d1_normal_user_fetch_probe.log`). Cloning as the normal user would therefore need that harness environment setting instead. **Impact:** file ownership only; no source, option or environment value of the build or run changes. **Not redone:** re-cloning would delete a tree that other workflows read (`../baselines/*.md` cite it) and would not change any build input. The PI may ask for it. |
| D-2 | README L107 `make native_std.lcov` | Not run | README L107; README L143 ("Requires/depends on "runtest" completing and passing"); `local-test.mk` L17-40 | deviation (requirement not met, no workaround applied) | `lcov` and `genhtml` are not installed (B4), and C12 did not pass, which L143 requires. Installing `lcov` would add an unreferenced package. **Impact:** no coverage data; binaries and runs are unaffected. The earlier D-2 also covered L106; that step has now been run (C12), so the earlier reason ("tests would run in the same staged tree") no longer applies, and it was inaccurate anyway (C12 notes). |
| D-3 | `/proc/schedstat` | Missing in this VM kernel | PSP module `linux_sysmon` (`psp/fsw/pc-linux/psp_module_list.cmake` L9) opens `/proc/schedstat` (`psp/fsw/modules/linux_sysmon/linux_sysmon.c` L321-325) | deviation (requirement not met, no workaround applied) | **Observed in every run:** `open(/proc/schedstat): No such file or directory`, `HS_SysMonInit(): Unable to start device 0110ff05`, HS event 74 "Error in system monitor initialization, RC=0xC8000005". **Impact:** `HS_AppInit` returns early (`apps/hs/fsw/src/hs_app.c` L333-341), so `HS_AppMain` skips `CFE_ES_WaitForStartupSync`, the watchdog enable and the event-monitor subscriptions (L74-125); HS still enters its main loop. HS CPU-utilisation monitoring is unavailable, and HS's startup synchronisation differs from a host with `/proc/schedstat`. Fixing it needs a kernel with `CONFIG_SCHEDSTATS`. **The bundle knows this failure:** its CI filters it out as a known issue, "the HS system monitor may not initialize depending on platform support" (`test-cfs-qemu.yml` L262-268). |
| D-4 | Root mode ("flight-like" alternative) | Not usable here without a further change. As root, OSAL does not read `msg_max` (`bsp_start.c` L66-78: only when `geteuid() != 0`), so it truncates nothing even in permissive mode (`os-impl-queues.c` L59-63, L102-105). `mq_open` with a depth above `msg_max` then needs `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE`, which this container removes even from root (`capsh --print`: "Current: =ep cap_sys_resource-ep", "Current IAB: !cap_sys_resource"; `CapEff 000001fffeffffff`). Root does have `CAP_SYS_NICE`, so RT priorities would work. | `logs/f_root_capability_probe.log`; `/home/user/work/procrace/cfs_nonref_attempt/runs/run01_root_plain.log` L7 ("Selected policy 2 for RT tasks", no `EPERM`) and L41, L49 (`OS_QueueCreate Error. errno = 22 (Invalid argument)`) | unspecified_by_reference (a limitation of a mode that is not in use; recorded, nothing applied) | A root run would need either `fs.mqueue.msg_max` ≥ 50 (the largest requested depth) or `CAP_SYS_RESOURCE`. Either is a change of host or container settings, so it would be a deviation, unless a case reference prescribes it. This corrects `ENV.md` §1, which blamed the root failure on the missing permissive mode of the non-reference `sample_defs`. |

Measurements, not settings. Method, references and all tables: `BASELINE_MEASURE.md`; data: `logs/m1_*`.
